SOC 1 Type 2 – Operative has several products that are audited and comply with the AICPA standards for Controls at a Service Organization, audited annually. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Operative maintains disaster recovery capabilities to minimize the impact of disruptions to our operations. Incident Response Operative implements a robust alert and monitoring solution to continuously identify potential cyber security incidents. Dedicated Incident Response personnel are on call 24/7 to ensure that security incidents are managed end-to-end. It sets out the steps taken by the Operative group of companies during the financial year ending 31 December 2026 to ensure that modern slavery and human trafficking are not taking place within our business or supply chains. This statement has been approved by the Board of Directors of Operative and will be reviewed and updated annually. About Operative Operative (comprising SintecMedia, NYC, Inc., SintecMedia Ltd., and their affiliates and subsidiaries, collectively “Operative”) is a global software company providing revenue management solutions and services to converged media companies worldwide. We operate primarily in low-risk jurisdictions and do not manufacture or sell physical goods. Our workforce is predominantly professional and knowledge-based, operating across office, home, and hybrid environments. We have operations and employees in the following regions: United States United Kingdom Australia Canada Brazil India Israel Romania Netherlands Our Commitment Operative has a zero-tolerance approach to modern slavery and human trafficking in all its forms, including forced labour, debt bondage, child labour, servitude, and human trafficking. We are committed to acting ethically and with integrity across all our business activities and to implementing effective systems and controls to ensure that modern slavery does not occur anywhere in our organisation or supply chains. We expect the same standards from all suppliers, contractors, and business partners who work with us or on our behalf. Polices and Governance Operative maintains a suite of policies that underpin our commitment to preventing modern slavery, including: Anti-Slavery Policy – sets out our zero-tolerance approach and the obligations of all colleagues and business partners Code of Ethics & Conflict of Interest Policy – establishes the ethical standards expected of all employees Diversity, Equality & Inclusion Policy – promotes fair and ethical treatment of all individuals Whistleblowing / Reporting Policy – provides safe and confidential channels for raising concerns All policies are approved by senior management, communicated to employees upon joining Operative, and reviewed periodically. Every new employee is required to read, acknowledge, and sign the Anti-Slavery Policy as part of their onboarding. Risk Assessment and Due Diligence Following a review of our operations and supply chain, we consider the overall risk of modern slavery within our business to be low. Operative is a technology and services company and does not operate in manufacturing, agriculture, or other sectors generally considered higher risk. However, we remain vigilant and maintain oversight of the following areas: Office and Facilities Services: Cleaning, catering, and other facilities services are typically managed by our property managers. Where we have the ability to influence contractual terms, we seek to include provisions requiring appropriate measures to address modern slavery risks within their operations and those of their subcontractors. Third-Party Contractors and Staffing Agencies: Where we engage workers through third-party providers, we seek assurances that such providers comply with applicable anti-slavery and labour laws and, where appropriate, our Anti-Slavery Policy. Service agreements may include modern slavery and labour compliance provisions depending on the nature of the engagement and the parties’ contracting arrangements. Procurement and Supply Chain: We take a risk-based approach to supplier management. Where appropriate, we seek to include human rights and labour compliance provisions in supplier agreements and apply enhanced scrutiny to suppliers operating in higher-risk jurisdictions. New and existing suppliers may be assessed on a risk-proportionate basis. Where potential risks are identified, we may take appropriate action, including seeking remediation, increasing monitoring, or, where appropriate, terminating the relationship. Awareness All Operative employees are required to read and sign our Anti-Slavery Policy upon joining and on a recurring annual policy update basis.
